sentences.text: Germanodactylus is a type of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Upper Jurassic period in Germany, known for its distinctive head crest.
Its robust maxillary teeth remain large in size even as they move away from the front of the jaw, unlike those of Pterodactylus.
The skull features a nasoantorbital fenestra that is twice as long as the eye orbit.
The beak was long and narrow with few or no teeth, ending in a horny extension at the tip.

Scientists first described the soft-tissue component of the head crest in 2002, suggesting it was made of cornified epidermis, a rare find that marks the first known instance of such a structure in a pterosaur genus.
G. cristatus had a wingspan of 0.98 meters and a skull measuring 13 centimeters, while G. rhamphastinus was slightly larger with a 1.08-meter wingspan and a 21-centimeter skull.
A tentatively referred hindlimb implies that G. cristatus could have grown larger than the currently known specimens.
The first fossils, which were impressions of the animal in limestone, were discovered in 1892 in rocks that now form part of Germany.

The type species G. cristatus is based on specimen BSP 1892.IV.1 from the Solnhofen limestone of Eichstätt, originally described by Plieninger in 1901 as Pterodactylus kochi before Carl Wiman named it G. cristatus in 1925, and Yang Zhongjian elevated it to its own genus in 1964.

The species G. rhamphastinus was originally described by Johann Andreas Wagner in 1851 as a species of the genus Ornithocephalus based on specimen BSP AS.I.745 from the Mörnsheimer Limestone of Daiting, and Peter Wellnhofer included it in the genus Germanodactylus in 1970.
Yang Zhongjian established the family Germanodactylidae for the genus, which belongs to the parent group Lophocratia and the class Reptilia.
Bennett placed the genus in the family Pterodactylidae, while Alexander W.A. Kellner found it related to Pterodactylus in his 2003 analysis.
In 2017, Vidovic and Martill created the new genus Altmuehlopterus for G. rhamphastinus.
It lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian, between 154.8 and 145.06 million years ago.
It is debated whether G. rhamphastinus deserves its own genus, "Daitingopterus", as suggested by Maisch and coauthors.
Bennett suggested in 1996 that Germanodactylus represented adults of Pterodactylus, but this hypothesis was later rejected by further studies.
